name: Trent Ltd
about: Trent Ltd is engaged in retailing of apparels, footwear, accessories, toys, games, food, grocery & non food products through various of its retail formats/ concepts. [1]

flags.text: Share capital up 47% in three years: new shares from an issue, a merger or a bonus. Only the first two dilute

business.what: Trent Limited runs large-format fashion retail chains, mainly Zudio (value fashion) and Westside, plus other lifestyle concepts, mostly through company-operated stores in India and three UAE cities. It earns revenue from store sales, including online sales through Westside and Tata Neu.

segments.name: Zudio (value fashion stores)
segments.comment: 22 stores opened in Q1; over 80% of new stores in Tier II/III cities.

segments.name: Westside (lifestyle fashion stores and online)
segments.comment: Only 1 store opened; online exceeded 6% of Westside revenue, growing profitably.

segments.name: Other lifestyle concepts (incl. Burnt Toast, Samoh)
segments.comment: 29 stores; newer brands at varying stages, with economics still being calibrated.

ledger.promise: Store openings to run at about 250 a year; judge on the annual rate, not quarterly counts
ledger.quote: Quarterly store openings are inherently asymmetric given the complexities around property development, fitout timelines, and regulatory approvals, and therefore the annual run rate is more representative.
ledger.actual: Store counts are not in the materials. FY26 investing outflow was 1,577 vs 923 in FY25, which fits continued expansion but does not prove the rate.

ledger.promise: FY27 store openings to stay broadly in line with the Chairman's outlook from the shareholders meeting
ledger.quote: On an annual basis we expect the trajectory of new store openings to remain broadly consistent in line with the outlook shared by the Chairman in the shareholders meeting.
ledger.actual: FY27 is not over. The Chairman's number is not in the materials, and no store counts are given.

ledger.promise: Speed up investment in store upgrades, new brands/categories/geographies, supply chain/warehousing, digital/automation and real estate for Star
ledger.quote: The intent is to accelerate select investments including (i) upgrade of our existing portfolio of stores (ii) commitment towards incubating new brands/categories/geographies (iii) expansion and automation of supply chain/warehouse capacity
ledger.actual: No amount was given. FY27 cash flow is not reported. FY26 investing outflow was 1,577 vs 923 in FY25 (+71%). FY27 CWIP is 238 vs 254.

ledger.promise: Raise equity (rights issue or otherwise) to fund the faster investment; timing to be evaluated
ledger.quote: Timelines for the aforesaid capital raising program, through issue of equity shares including through rights issue or otherwise, would be evaluated and pursued in due course.
ledger.actual: The Q1 FY27 call gives no update. Borrowings were 2,328 in FY27 vs 2,561 in FY26. The materials do not show a raise being completed.

ledger.promise: Newer tier 2/3 and metro-periphery stores will mature over two to three years, lifting like-for-like growth
ledger.quote: Many of these markets are still evolving in terms of adoption of fashion trends and density of consumption.
ledger.actual: Fashion like-for-like was low single digits in Q2 FY26, marginally negative in Q3 FY26 and low single digits in FY26. The 2–3 year window, first stated Q4 FY26, has not passed.

ledger.promise: Weak Q3 FY26 like-for-like growth was partly a festive-timing shift, implying it would recover
ledger.quote: Like-for-like growth for our fashion portfolio in Q3FY26 was marginally negative, in part due to the shift in the festive period.
ledger.actual: Q4 FY26 and FY26 like-for-like stayed only low single digits (Q4 FY26 call p10). Q4 FY26 revenue still grew 19.2% (5,028 vs 4,217).

ledger.promise: Food & Grocery revenue held back by store upgrades (Q2 FY26 879 vs 898), implying it would recover after the upgrades
ledger.quote: *Multiple stores underwent upgrade in Q2 and H1; Revenue Includes Zudio SIS stores
ledger.actual: No later Food & Grocery segment revenue is in the materials.

ledger.promise: CSR cotton programme: reach about 3,000 tribal cotton-growing households over 1,500–1,800 acres in 30 villages
ledger.quote: is aimed to promote ecological sound, and economically viable cotton production to 3,000 small and marginal farming families (primarily tribal).
ledger.actual: The Q4 FY26 call reports 200 households reached so far (about 7% of 3,000). The Q1 FY27 call repeats the target with no new count. No deadline was set.

ledger.promise: CSR water programme: add 20.93 million cubic feet of water storage, bringing 2,114 acres under irrigation
ledger.quote: The program aims to enhance water conservation capacity upto 20.93 Million Cubic Feet bringing 2114 acres under protective irrigation.
ledger.actual: The target was repeated on the Q3 FY26 call. No progress figure is reported.

ledger.promise: CSR: raise women artisans' monthly income by 50%
ledger.quote: assisted with market linkages to help increase their monthly income levels by 50%.

ledger.promise: Support an additional 50 Trent Scholars every year
ledger.quote: Trent remains committed to supporting an additional 50 scholars every year through internships, mentorship, books, certifications, workshops, living expenses, and a full-time psychologist.
ledger.actual: This is an ongoing annual commitment. No count is reported yet.

current_guidance.target: Annual pace broadly in line with the Chairman's outlook (about 250 a year per the Q4 FY26 call); no quarterly target
current_guidance.quote: On an annual basis we expect the trajectory of new store openings to remain broadly consistent in line with the outlook shared by the Chairman in the shareholders meeting.

current_guidance.target: No number given. Middle East disruption could affect supply chain, commodity prices and inflation
current_guidance.quote: the duration and intensity of disruptions in the Middle East along with its second order effect on supply chain, commodity prices and inflation in general has potential near term implications.

current_guidance.target: Newer markets mature over two to three years
current_guidance.quote: Our experience indicates that newer markets tend to mature over a two-to-three year period.

current_guidance.target: Faster investment in five named areas; no amount
current_guidance.quote: The intent is to accelerate select investments including (i) upgrade of our existing portfolio of stores (ii) commitment towards incubating new brands/categories/geographies (iii) expansion and automation of supply chain/warehouse capacity

current_guidance.target: Equity issue, including a possible rights issue; no size or timing
current_guidance.quote: Timelines for the aforesaid capital raising program, through issue of equity shares including through rights issue or otherwise, would be evaluated and pursued in due course.

credibility.label: too early
credibility.summary: Across four calls management gave no numeric targets for revenue, margin, profit or capex. The only financial-style commitments (store-opening pace, faster investment, an equity raise) have no numbers, and the materials cannot yet settle them. The one testable implied claim, that weak Q3 FY26 like-for-like was partly festive timing, was not followed by a like-for-like recovery in Q4 FY26. Reported revenue and margins still grew, so there are no clear misses on headline numbers, but there is also little stated guidance to measure against.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Q3 FY26 was hurt by the GST transition, muted consumer sentiment and an early festive season, with fashion like-for-like marginally negative.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Q3 FY26 revenue rose 14.8% (5,345 vs 4,657) and EBITDA margin hit a high of 20.2% (vs 18.2%). PAT rose only 2.6% (510 vs 497), so the weakness showed up in profit after EBITDA, not in revenue or margin.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Low like-for-like growth reflects newer tier 2/3 stores that are not yet comparable and take 2–3 years to mature, not weakness in the core business.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Revenue growth slowed from 38.5% in FY25 (17,135 vs 12,375) to 17.2% in FY26 (20,074) while expansion continued. H1 FY27 revenue grew 19.9% (11,628 vs 9,701). Like-for-like data to test the maturity claim is not provided.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Equity capital is needed to fund faster investment in stores, supply chain, digital and real estate.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: FY26 cash from operations of 2,668 covered investing outflow of 1,577 with about 1,091 left over. Borrowings fell from 2,561 (FY26) to 2,328 (FY27). Reported cash flows do not yet show a funding gap.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Middle East disruption could have near-term effects on supply chain, commodities and inflation.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 18.0% from 19.4% in Q1 FY27 and PBT fell to 619 from 692. On a year-on-year basis, though, the margin was up from 16.9% and revenue rose 21.9% (5,873 vs 4,818).

bull.point: Margins have widened while the company expands
Cash generation and working capital are improving
bull.evidence: Cash from operations rose 60.6% to 2,668 in FY26 from 1,661. The cash conversion cycle fell from 45 days (FY24) to 43 (FY25) to 36 (FY26), and inventory days fell from 83 to 74.

bull.point: Growth sped up in H1 FY27 despite the risks management flagged
bull.evidence: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21.9% (5,873 vs 4,818) and PAT rose 25.5% (468 vs 373). Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17.9% and PAT 21.9%. TTM PAT is 1,909 vs FY26's 1,721.

bear.point: Core like-for-like growth has been weak for several quarters, and the recovery story rests on an untested 2–3 year maturity claim
bear.evidence: Fashion like-for-like was low single digits in Q2 FY26, marginally negative in Q3 FY26 and low single digits in Q4 FY26/FY26. Management keeps pointing to new-store dilution.
bear.source: Q3 FY26 call p8; Q4 FY26 call p10

bear.point: EBITDA gains are not turning into profit at the same rate
bear.evidence: FY26 EBITDA grew 32.8% (3,745 vs 2,820) but PAT grew only 12.2% (1,721 vs 1,534). In Q3 FY26, EBITDA rose 27.6% while PAT rose 2.6%.

bear.point: Faster capex plus a planned equity issue could dilute shareholders, with no amount or return target given
bear.evidence: Management plans to speed up investment in five areas and to raise equity 'including through rights issue or otherwise'. FY26 investing outflow already rose 71% to 1,577. Q1 FY27 also flagged Middle East risk to costs.
bear.source: Q4 FY26 call p11; Q1 FY27 call p9
